thread:
Sam (Sales): Hey team — ACMECloud POC just sent back a blocker. They require BYO-CMK via their CloudHSM, need rotation windows, attestation artifacts, and a rough pricing delta. Can we answer by EOD?
Priya (Solutions Eng): Do we support CloudHSM BYO for Redwood Private? Any perf/throughput caveats we should call out?
Ethan (Crypto Ops): Yes — two supported modes: proxy-mode (Redwood key-proxy talks to customer HSM) or direct-networked HSM. Proxy-mode = lower onboarding time, small extra latency (~3–8ms per KMS call) but we can do batching; direct-mode depends on customer's HSM throughput.
Ethan (Crypto Ops): Quick example flow:
```
Client -> Redwood Private -> (mTLS) -> Customer CloudHSM
Master CMK stored only in customer HSM; Redwood caches derived DEKs (KV cache) for token lifetime.
Rotation: master CMK rotate window scheduled (recommended) 02:00-03:00 UTC, 30m maintenance window.
```
Priya (Solutions Eng): Good — can we support daily rotation for derived/ephemeral keys? Customer asked for sub-24h TTL.
Ethan (Crypto Ops): Yes for derived/session keys. Master CMK rotation more heavyweight — we recommend >=7 days for hot rolling, monthly for standard. Config knobs: rotate_master_days (integer), derived_ttl_seconds.
Claire (Security): For the security questionnaire: we can provide HSM attestation certs (CloudHSM/SKSM cert chain), per-request audit logs, and evidence that we never export master plaintext. We will supply: HSM cert bundle, mTLS fingerprint, logging sample, and our key-handling diagram.
Claire (Security): Example answer snippet to Q12 (key custody): "Customer-managed master keys are generated and stored in the customer's HSM. Redwood performs cryptographic operations via authenticated channel; we do not retain master key material. Audit logs include key usage events with request IDs."
Maya (Legal): Note — procurement wants an explicit escrow/exception clause. Our standard is: we do not escrow customer keys. Any exception requires a signed SOW + court-ordered process. I'll draft a 1-paragraph addendum.
Sam (Sales): Pricing ask: they want delta vs standard hosted. Can we give bullets?
Ethan (Crypto Ops): Rough pricing examples (ballpark to share now):
- One-time integration/onboarding fee: $5,000
- BYO-HSM connector monthly: $1,200 (management + monitoring)
- Per-key-op surcharge (if using HSM ops directly): ~$0.02/op; bulk commits (reserved throughput) reduce to $0.006/op
- If customer uses proxy-mode and we cache DEKs, per-op surcharge may be lower.
Priya (Solutions Eng): Also call out SLA: Dedicated throughput SLA still applies for token gen, but BYO-HSM adds dependency — we recommend a canary + fallback to a Redwood-managed model variant for degraded HSM connectivity. Include fallback policy in SOW.
Sam (Sales): Can someone paste a short SOW paragraph I can drop in the quote?
Ethan (Crypto Ops): SOW snippet: "Redwood will integrate with Customer-provided HSM (CloudHSM). Integration includes connector setup, attestation verification, and testing of rotation procedures. Redwood will perform cryptographic operations without exporting master key material. A 30-day onboarding and validation window is included; additional engineering time billed at standard hourly rates."
Claire (Security): Add on the ops checklist for procurement: attestation cert, network allowlist (IPs), mTLS CA, expected QPS per region, and rotation schedule.
Sam (Sales): Can you paste the network allowlist and minimal firewall requirements? I can forward to their infra team.
Priya (Solutions Eng): Minimal: outbound TLS to customer's HSM endpoints on port 443, source IPs: 52.14.20.0/24, 44.12.11.0/24 (add to SOW to confirm final). mTLS client certs we exchange during onboarding.
Ethan (Crypto Ops): Also include a short test plan for the POC: generate 100k key ops over 24h, test failover (simulate HSM downtime), test rotation with a preflight dry-run.
DeployBot: Ticket created INF-4721 for BYO-HSM onboarding and POC runbook; assigned to @Ethan.
Maya (Legal): I uploaded a terse escrow clause draft to the deal folder. Will tag you, @Sam.
Sam (Sales): Great. One more — procurement wants liability / SLA impact if customer HSM is down during business hours. What do we tell them?
Priya (Solutions Eng): We should say: Redwood provides best-effort retries and configurable fallbacks. If customer HSM is unavailable, calls will fail and customers can: (a) use cached DEKs until TTL; (b) route to a Redwood-managed compatible model if agreed in fallbacks. Any availability guarantees for crypto ops depend on customer's HSM uptime and are excluded from Redwood's HSM SLA unless a dedicated uplink/resiliency commit is in place.
Ethan (Crypto Ops): Suggest offering an optional HA design: dual-HSM (customer primary + backup) or cross-region replicate; that raises onboarding and monthly fees but gives clear RTO/RPO.
Sam (Sales): Perfect. I'll send these bullets + SOW snippet to ACMECloud procurement now. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Priya (Solutions Eng): Marking checklist items: attestation cert, network allowlist, test plan, pricing bullets. I'll keep sync with INF-4721.
Ethan (Crypto Ops): Ping me if they want specific perf numbers for their HSM model.
Sam (Sales): Closing loop — will update thread with customer reply.
